segments.title: Chương 86: 0086【Thiếu nữ đa cảm】
segments.content:
After all the running around in the city and county, Chen Guiliang returned to the village for more.

If not for the gongs and drums that day, Chen Guiliang wouldn't have had to host a banquet at all. But since the news had already spread and so many people had come to celebrate, it would have been improper not to treat the villagers to a meal.

The spread was quite lavish; he hadn't intended to make money from the gift money.

After settling the accounts, he had actually lost several hundred yuan.

His parents and grandma were especially happy because all the villagers were saying pleasant things, and their family was now one of the most prominent in the village.

After the village banquet, things finally quieted down, and Chen Guiliang read the History of the Ming Dynasty at home in peace.

During this time, he also made a trip to the city to buy air conditioners for his home and his maternal grandmother's home.

It's so hot!

The major newspapers were once again boosting Chen Guiliang's fame.

When dozens of media outlets came last time, Principal Yan had given the reporters his phone number, so now they could interview him directly over the phone.

On the phone with reporters from various papers, Principal Yan repeated over and over again: "Chen Guiliang is a very talented student. His middle school entrance exam scores were among the best in the city. Although his high school grades declined at one point, it was because he was engrossed in literature, history, and philosophy books. He's a left-behind child from a relatively poor family, and he would rather go hungry to buy books."

"At its worst, Chen Guiliang's grades fell below the Tier 2 university cut-off score. After learning from this painful experience, he sold all his extracurricular books and focused wholeheartedly on sprinting for the Gaokao, studying anytime and anywhere. Heaven does not disappoint the diligent. Student Chen Guiliang's grades in his senior year improved with every test. Finally, in the Gaokao, he surpassed Peking University's submission line by 8 points!"

The "submission line" from Principal Yan's mouth became the "admission line" in the reporters' articles.

And so, one report after another was published.

Moreover, Han Han, who had dropped out due to failing subjects, was dug up again by reporters to be publicly shamed, serving as a negative example to highlight Chen Guiliang.

As a result, Chen Guiliang attracted more attention nationwide than the top scorers from any province.

Because the story was so sensational: a student specially recruited by Peking University could actually get in on his own merit!

Evening.

The moon rose, and the stars appeared.

Even with an air conditioner at home, they were reluctant to use it. His parents and grandma carried stools and cattail leaf fans to chat and cool off with the neighbors under the big tree.

Chen Guiliang, on the other hand, moved two long benches to set up a cooling spot in his own courtyard, lit a mosquito coil, and lay under the night sky watching the stars.

After 8 PM, a gentle breeze blew in, carrying away some of the summer heat.

The mountains and fields across the river were shrouded in the night, and the towering archway of the abandoned pier could be vaguely seen. The moonlight and stars reflected on the jade-belt-like river, and the river breeze made the poplar leaves and bamboo grove rustle.

The chirping of insects and croaking of frogs rose and fell, yet it made the night seem even more tranquil.

Under the distant big tree, a burst of laughter occasionally erupted, who knows what amusing topic the people were discussing.

The rice was about to ripen and could be harvested in a little over half a month; it seemed one could faintly smell its fragrance.

Chen Guiliang gazed at the brilliant starry sky, his mind completely empty. It felt as if he could communicate with all things in heaven and earth, that he had become one with nature.

In that instant, Chen Guiliang recalled Zhang Xiaoxiang's lines: "Scoop up all of the West River, pour it from the Northern Dipper, and treat all creation as my guests. Tapping the boat's side, I whistle alone, unknowing what night this is!"

These days were truly leisurely and pleasant.

Then, the phone rang.

"I got my admission notice," said Bian Guanyue.

Chen Guiliang said: "Which school did you apply to anyway? You've been so secretive."

Bian Guanyue said: "I wasn't sure before. My dad paid an expert to seriously analyze all the schools in Beijing. The expert said the best choice was the Capital University of Economics and Business. This school is going to become a Tier 1 university in a few years."

"What major?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Bian Guanyue said: "Public Administration."

Chen Guiliang said: "Hmm... that's not bad, suits you well."

Bian Guanyue said: "This year, 28% of CUEB's undergraduate programs are Tier 1, and 72% are Tier 2. Popular majors like economics, finance, insurance, and international trade all require scores above the Tier 1 line. There were only two Tier 2 majors I liked, Public Administration and Communications, but the expert said many people would definitely rush to apply for them. Hehe, it was a close call, but luckily I got in."

"Congratulations," Chen Guiliang offered his sincere congratulations. "That expert was right. In a few years, CUEB will definitely be promoted to Tier 1."

Bian Guanyue asked: "When does Peking University start?"

Chen Guiliang said: "New students register on August 19th, and military training starts on the 22nd."

"CUEB is around the same time. Let's fly there together," Bian Guanyue joked. "You must have a lot of money now, with royalties and Gaokao prize money."

Chen Guiliang said: "Still remember the one thousand yuan I owe you for clothes?"

"Of course I remember. Don't you dare go back on your word," Bian Guanyue said, then grew sentimental. "We hadn't known each other for long back then, and in a flash, we're both about to start university. Time really flies."

Chen Guiliang asked: "You haven't lost the keepsake from the First Emperor of Qin, have you?"

"Hmph, lost it long ago. I don't care for your stupid rock," Bian Guanyue's tone was somewhere between coquettish and proud.

Chen Guiliang chuckled: "Then that's quite a big loss for you."

As they chatted about random things, Bian Guanyue suddenly blurted out: "Do you know my pet name?"

"Suobianbian (to shrink back from things, to shirk responsibility)?" Chen Guiliang teased.

Bian Guanyue feigned anger: "You're the one who's a suobianbian! The elders in my family all call me Guanguan."

Chen Guiliang played the perfect straight man: "Why not Bianbian or Yueyue?"

Bian Guanyue explained: "My family's surname is already Bian, so naturally no one calls me Bianbian. Also, I have a relative whose pet name is Yueyue. So my grandparents started calling me Guanguan, and it slowly became my pet name. Even my maternal grandparents call me that."

"I still think Suobianbian sounds better," Chen Guiliang said.

Bian Guanyue reiterated: "You're not allowed to call me Suobianbian. That was a random nickname my elementary school classmates gave me!"

Chen Guiliang knew what Bian Guanyue meant; she just wanted him to call her by her pet name from now on.

But he just had to tease her.

Men are all childish fools!

"Guanguan."

"Mhm."

Over the next few days, Chen Guiliang received a series of phone calls.

Xu Haibo was successfully admitted to Sichuan University, a situation that hadn't changed.

Xie Yang, however, had changed completely.

In the other timeline, Xie Yang had barely passed the Tier 2 line and went to study in Huludao.

In this timeline, spurred on by Chen Guiliang, Xie Yang would study seriously for a few days here and there, and in the final month, he completely settled down to review.

He ended up scoring in the upper-middle range of Tier 2 and chose to study accounting at Hangzhou Dianzi University.

This school had just been renamed. It used to be jokingly called "Hangzhou Electrical Engineering," giving the impression of connecting wires and changing electricity meters. This year it was renamed Hangzhou Dianzi University, which instantly gave it more prestige, and it was quite popular when students were filling out their applications.

The class president, Li Rui, was admitted to Renmin University and was also going to study in Beijing.

Wang Siyu went to a Tier 3 institution.

Li Yulin and Wang Yu flew off together, both going to a Tier 2 university in the Mountain City. Li Yulin even said on the phone that he planned to marry Wang Yu right after graduation.

Wishing them all the best.

Fan Junfei, who had been on good terms with Chen Guiliang before the arts and sciences streams were separated but had little contact since choosing science, somehow got Chen Guiliang's number and called.

This guy went to Harbin Institute of Technology.

It was quite absurd. He played video games even more crazily than Xie Yang and also read literature with Chen Guiliang. It was only in his senior year that he secluded himself to study hard and somehow got into HIT.

Chen Guiliang's social circle was genuinely good; more than 30 people called him one after another.

Most were classmates from the arts stream, but there were also some old classmates from his first year who were now in the science stream.

In mid-August, Bian Guanyue returned to the county town to stay with her maternal grandparents for a few days, and then she would go to Beijing with Chen Guiliang.

She had wanted to ask Wu Meng and Li Rui to join them, but those two chose to take the train.

The day before leaving home.

Yao Lan was frantically stuffing things into his suitcase.

"Mom, what are you packing spicy sauce for?" Chen Guiliang didn't know whether to laugh or cry.

Yao Lan said: "You won't be able to get this flavor in Beijing."

"I really don't need it," Chen Guiliang said.

Yao Lan thought it over and reluctantly took out the few jars of spicy sauce.

Grandma was getting eggs to boil. Chen Guiliang quickly said: "Just boil two or three. I'll take them to eat at the airport."

Chen Xinghua asked: "Are you sure you don't need us to see you off?"

Chen Guiliang said: "Seeing me off from the village is enough, no need to go to the station. You should stay home and thresh the grain."

The rice was already ripe.

The next day, Second Uncle and his maternal grandfather's family also came to see him off, but none of them accompanied him out of the village.

Because his dad had called for the village's motorcycle taxi, Chen Guiliang went directly to the long-distance bus station on the motorcycle.

"I'm leaving. Goodbye!" Chen Guiliang waved to everyone.

"Meow~~"

Panda had actually followed them.

As the motorcycle rode further and further away, Chen Guiliang looked back and could only see a small black figure.

He felt a sudden pang of sadness.

"I just got off the taxi outside the bus station."

"I'm in the waiting hall. I've already bought your ticket."

"Okay, I'll be right there."

There were several people sitting in the waiting hall.

Besides Chen Guiliang, there were also his cousin-uncle, cousin-aunt, Tao Xue, and Yang Yuhui.

"Brother Yang, you've stayed behind?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Yang Yuhui said: "I'll keep running the private server and the workshop here, and help Brother Gang manage the internet cafes on the side. Once most of the internet cafes are sold, I'll go to Hangzhou to meet up with Brother Gang."

Chen Guiliang then asked Feng Tao: "Cousin-uncle, aren't you going over?"

Feng Tao had little ambition: "Staying in my hometown is pretty good. Brother Gang promised to transfer his 80% share in the computer store to me in stages. I'll work hard to earn the money and buy the shop."

Chen Guiliang didn't try to persuade him. It was a personal choice, and persuasion would be useless.

Tao Xue kept her head down without speaking. Perhaps because their separation was near, she couldn't bring herself to be her usual lively self.

After a long silence, Tao Xue took out a cassette tape: "Jay Chou's Qi Li Xiang. I just bought it. It's really good, this is for you."

"Thanks," Chen Guiliang said. "You have to work hard too."

Tao Xue made a vow: "I'm going to get into Peking University. When the time comes, you'll still be my senior, and I'll still be your junior!"

Chen Guiliang laughed out loud: "Good luck."

He didn't take it seriously. Peking University wasn't a place you could get into just by saying so.

Just then, Yang Yuhui exclaimed: "Whoa, what a great beauty!"

Bian Guanyue walked over, pulling a suitcase and waving at them.

Chen Guiliang's eyes also lit up. Bian Guanyue had specially put on makeup today, making her look even more radiant, enchanting, and utterly stunning.

She was prettier than many female celebrities.

Tao Xue instantly felt insecure, feeling as if Chen Guiliang was about to drift further and further away from her.

Only when the long-distance bus was about to depart did Tao Xue timidly pull out a pair of gloves, her eyes red as if she was about to cry: "Senior, I won't take advantage of you anymore, I won't call you big nephew anymore. I... I haven't been learning for long, my knitting skills aren't good. If you don't like them, just don't wear them."

The skill was indeed quite poor. The stitches were uneven, and the two gloves weren't even the same size.

But Tao Xue had knitted them with her own hands, stitch by stitch.

Chen Guiliang accepted them solemnly and patted her on the head, saying: "An elder can't cry. Give me a smile, Auntie Xue."

Tao Xue pouted: "Don't pat my head, it'll make me dumb, and I'm not smart to begin with."

Bian Guanyue looked up at the clock on the station wall, pretending she didn't know what had just happened.

She decided that when winter came, she would also knit a pair of gloves for Chen Guiliang!

On second thought, a scarf would be better, so he wouldn't have to choose.

The ticket inspector was already urging them, so Bian Guanyue pulled up her suitcase and left.

Tao Xue said goodbye to Chen Guiliang, then waved and called out: "Goodbye, Senior Sister."

Bian Guanyue turned with a smile: "Goodbye, Junior Sister."

Tao Xue watched them put their luggage on the bus, watched the bus slowly start to move, watched it gradually recede into the distance... Her eyes reddened again. She wasn't like this before.

Yang Yuhui gave a thumbs-up and said in a low voice: "Two beauties. Your nephew is awesome!"

(Seems like there's double monthly ticket event? Weakly asking for one.)
